lines.text: Bread. Fifty. For everybody's face. Eat.
Saturday is a long night. I hear.
I couldn't say it. Who would believe a shopkeeper?
So I priced it.
For your face today? Free. I listen to the radio.
The other radio.
Welcome! For your face today? Everything is negotiable. Except bread.
My customer! Your face is fine today. Prices are fine too.
Ah. That face. That face pays full price.
How far? [How are you?] Look at the board before you talk.
Go well! Come back when your face is happier.
Bye. Prices change at sunset. So do faces.
Thank me? Thank your face. It got the discount.
No credit. Credit is a different shop. It closed.
Discount? Your face is not in the mood for discount.
Who? There was nobody there fa. You want something or not?
Price by mood. Today my mood is: rent.
Same item, two prices? One is for you. One is for your friend's face.
You have candles at home? …Just asking. Shopkeeper asking.
Light gone? Ehen. [I see.] You bought the batteries? No? Hm.
Shop is open. Bring your own light. And your own face.
Light! Batteries back to ₦200. Mood restored.
Rain! Umbrella ₦1,500. It's raining, my friend. Supply and demand.
Cold water ₦100. Warm water ₦50. Choose your suffering.
For your face today? ₦300.
Yesterday ₦200. Today ₦350. Tomorrow? Ask tomorrow.
Smile. …₦250. Smile again. …No, the first one was better.
Transfer? Network is in a meeting. Cash.
Indomie, ₦250. Indomie with my advice, ₦300.
Chalk! Box of it. You understand my business model.
A calculator? Fixed prices? You want to kill me?
A new blackboard. Big. …Now I can be twice as confusing.
Batteries, ₦900. …What? Batteries have feelings too.
Bread, ₦50. Today only. Don't ask why. Eat.
Candles, sold out. Since noon. Who knew?
Rewriting the board. Chalk is my only staff.
Radio says sunny. My radio says other things.
Torch, cheap today. Too cheap. Buy two anyway.
Matches, ₦5. Don't ask. I'm in a generous mood. Suddenly.
Late. Last loaf. Take it. Tonight, take it.
Table today, shop tomorrow. Tell your friend with the 'brand'.
Your friend sells chargers in a basement. I sell faces. Different market.
Grand opening! Prices by mood! Today my mood is: opening.
For your face? No. For the week. Batteries, triple.
The mall has escalators. I have a stool. Same function.
Free torch with that man's face? I charge less for no face.
Strike prices. Garri cheap. Patience expensive.
Bread, ₦50. Saturday is a long night. I hear.
Student in strike? For your face today? Half.
Famous face! Famous face pays famous price.
Kerosene up. Don't look at me like that. Look at the sky.
Eat now. Bread is half price. Now, not later.
Who would believe a shopkeeper? So I priced it.
True prices now. They're more boring. Batteries, ₦900.
The other radio. Still listening. For your face: free.
Batteries ₦200 every day now. I'm bored. Buy anyway.
Board is the same all week. Customers think I'm sick.
Freshers! New faces! New prices! Everybody, a fresh face price!
Exam week. Coffee ₦100. Rechargeable lamp, cheap. Read.
Allowance day! I can see it in your face. Prices up.
Strike. Stay-behind price. Don't tell anybody.
Christmas! Biscuits by the carton. Go home with a face.
Valentine. Chocolate by mood. Single face, discount.
Harmattan! Vaseline ₦400. Your lips are paying, not you.
